blindSummary: This is a serious-danger destination for trans visitors: same-sex conduct is legal (never criminalised), but a 2024 country-of-origin report by a regional asylum agency documents societal discrimination, police harassment and absence of protection; there is no legal gender recognition, and the community is small and underground.
blindOutOfScope: A regional asylum agency report documents the harassment pattern.
blindSourceSummaries: A regional asylum agency's country-of-origin query response (May 2024) on this country: the situation of LGBTIQ people, covering legislation and implementation, treatment by the state and society, availability of state protection, and access to support services, for January 2022 to May 2024. Same-sex conduct is not criminalised but public-expression provisions are applied; state protection is limited.
NOTE: This is a foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on a neighbouring state, fetched under this country's record; that report's SOGI section documents societal discrimination and violence.

A foreign government's 2022 human-rights report on this country: official assessment including the SOGI section - same-sex conduct not criminalised, but societal discrimination documented; no legal gender recognition.
A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report on this country: official assessment including the SOGI section - continuing societal discrimination and absence of protections.

A foreign government's 2010 human-rights report on this country: documents suspected killings of detainees, mob violence, rape, extortion by armed elements, poor prisons, and societal discrimination - general baseline.
NOTE: This is a foreign government's 2020 world-report index page (navigation only); the specific country report content was not retrievable.
